abstract: Understanding key biological processes governed by cell surface protein distribution requires highly multiplexed imaging. Binary barcode methods based on DNA hybridization represent a powerful approach to such imaging; however, higher multiplexing demands longer DNA barcodes, which substantially compromise localization resolution. Here we introduce circular DNA-based multiplexed DNA-PAINT (CircDNA-PAINT), a method that achieves a resolution better than 20 nm and thus enables robust binary encoded multiplexing. This approach avoids the linear time overhead of adaptor-cycling DNA-PAINT and greatly shortens acquisition time for large-plex imaging. CircDNA-PAINT provides a new tool for dissecting complex nanoscale cellular architectures.
